loading.learn: Learn about animals. Learn about nature.
loading.fact.fox_snow: A fox can hear a mouse moving under the snow. It leaps high and dives in nose first.
loading.fact.rabbit_babies: Baby rabbits are born blind and without fur. Baby hares are born furry, with their eyes open.
loading.fact.kestrel_uv: Kestrels can see ultraviolet light, which shows them the trails voles leave in the grass.
loading.fact.kestrel_hover: A kestrel can hang still in the air, facing into the wind, while it looks for food below.
loading.fact.bee_shiver: Bumblebees warm up by shivering their flight muscles, so they can fly on cold mornings.
loading.fact.bee_pollen: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower. That is how plants make seeds and berries.
loading.fact.pike_ambush: A pike waits without moving among the water plants, then strikes in a flash.
loading.fact.perch_stripes: Perch have dark stripes that help them hide among water plants. It is Finland's national fish.
loading.fact.bream_mud: Bream feed on the lake bottom, sucking tiny animals out of the mud.
loading.fact.dead_wood: A fallen tree is not wasted. Beetles, fungi, woodpeckers and many more live in old wood.
loading.fact.nuuksio: Nuuksio National Park is right next to Helsinki. Its symbol is the flying squirrel.
loading.help.distance: Keep your distance from wild animals and their young. Watching quietly is the best way to meet them.
loading.help.garden: Leave a corner of your garden wild. Flowers and long grass feed bees and butterflies.
loading.help.litter: Take your litter home. Plastic in nature can hurt animals for many years.
loading.help.pet_fish: Never let pet fish go in a lake. They can bring diseases and push out wild fish.
loading.help.trails: Stay on the trails in nature parks, so plants and nests don't get trampled.
